Welcome to Sturminster Newton High School
At Sturminster we set high standards for academic and personal achievement within the ethos of a smaller school setting. We are extremely proud of our school and value the size of our school community where staff and students know one another and where students are treated and valued as individuals.
As a small school based in Dorset, one of our strengths is that we know our students well and are able to help them succeed on a personal level. The school promotes a happy and purposeful teaching environment, where all are supported and encouraged to do their best.
We believe that happy students become successful learners, happy students develop the skills to succeed in life and that happy students learn to become independent and thoughtful adults. Young people leaving this school will be confident individuals with the necessary life skills for further success at university, college or in employment. We emphasise the development of good organisational, communication, ICT and problem-solving skills, thus developing young people who can use their initiative and relate well to others. In return, we expect good manners, a respect for the school and a positive attitude towards learning.
“The school has high expectations of behaviour”
Working in partnership with parents our combined aim is to build upon the existing standards and success, moving all aspects of school life to the highest possible levels. We believe in educating students academically, emotionally, socially and spiritually in order to support and challenge them to achieve their best.
In September we hold an open evening for parents/carers of children in school years 5 and 6 to visit and tour our school. If, you are a prospective parent, please do not hesitate to contact the school to arrange an individual visit. Our staff and students will be pleased to show you around the school and discuss provision with you.
If you have trouble finding any information please use the search button on the footer menu or contact us on our contact page.
“Pupils embrace the school’s values of respect, responsiblity and resilience”

Careers
At Sturminster Newton High School, our Careers Education curriculum is designed to ensure that all students are entitled to high-quality, impartial and accessible careers guidance, regardless of background or starting point. Rooted in our whole-school commitment to equity of provision and high expectations, our careers programme empowers students to make informed and aspirational choices about their futures.
Careers education is delivered through tutorial sessions and personalised guidance interviews. All students at Key Stages 4 and 5 receive a minimum of two individual careers interviews, ensuring tailored support that reflects their interests, strengths and ambitions. We deliberately make clear links between curriculum subjects and future pathways so that students understand how their learning connects to further education, training and employment.
Our curriculum aims to develop reflective, self-aware individuals who can identify their personal qualities, set goals and take ownership of their next steps. Through encounters with employers, universities, colleges and apprenticeship providers, students build valuable cultural capital and broaden their horizons. Parents and carers are supported through access to relevant information, including labour market insights, enabling them to guide students confidently.
The impact of our careers provision is measured through destination data and student voice. Ultimately, our careers curriculum ensures that every student leaves Sturminster Newton High School informed, confident and prepared for the next stage of their education or training.
Sturminster Newton High School is committed to ensuring that all young people have access to realistic information and guidance about the full range of career pathways available to them.
We aim to ensure that all our students are self-confident, skilled and career-ready.
This will be achieved through a programme of high quality, planned Careers and Work Related Learning activities, advice and guidance which meets the Gatsby Benchmarks for careers advice, namely:
A stable careers programme

Modern Foreign Languages
The Modern Foreign Languages curriculum is founded on the belief that every student is entitled to high expectations and equitable access to language learning. Through a carefully sequenced curriculum, students develop the confidence and competence to communicate effectively in another language.
Learning is structured to build vocabulary, grammar and phonics progressively, enabling students to understand and produce language accurately. Listening, speaking, reading and writing skills are developed in balance, with frequent opportunities to revisit and apply prior knowledge to new contexts.
The curriculum broadens students’ cultural awareness by exploring cultural differences, values and perspectives from other countries. This promotes curiosity, respect and understanding of the wider world, supporting students to see beyond their immediate experiences.
MFL develops resilience, memory and communication skills that are transferable across the curriculum. By the time students leave school, they are confident communicators with the linguistic and cultural knowledge needed for further study, travel and employment in an increasingly global society.

Drama
The Drama curriculum ensures that all students have access to a high-quality, inclusive and creatively ambitious education that values performance, collaboration and self-expression. High expectations support students to develop confidence and resilience through practical exploration.
The curriculum is carefully sequenced to build skills in acting, devising, directing and evaluation. Students explore a range of styles, techniques and theatrical forms, applying knowledge progressively through rehearsal and performance.
Collaboration is central to Drama. Students develop communication, teamwork and leadership skills while learning to reflect critically on their own work and the work of others. A supportive environment encourages risk-taking and creativity.
Drama supports personal development by building confidence, empathy and emotional literacy. By the time students leave school, they are articulate, reflective individuals equipped with transferable skills that support further study, employment and active participation in cultural life.

Music
The Music curriculum is built on the principle that music is for all, and that every student is entitled to an ambitious, inclusive and carefully sequenced musical education. Through high expectations and equitable access to musical experiences, students develop confidence, creativity and a lifelong appreciation of music.
The curriculum is structured around performance, composition, listening and music production, allowing students to build practical musicianship alongside secure musical knowledge. Learning is sequenced to develop understanding of musical elements, styles and contexts across a wide range of genres, cultures and historical periods. Music technology is embedded throughout, enabling students to create, refine and communicate musical ideas effectively.
As students progress, they develop increasing independence as performers and composers. Rehearsal, reflection and refinement are central to learning, encouraging resilience, discipline and ambition. Collaborative music-making supports communication and teamwork, while performance opportunities build confidence and self-expression.
Music plays a vital role in students’ personal development and wellbeing. By the time students leave school, they are equipped with musical understanding, cultural capital and transferable skills that prepare them for further study, enrichment opportunities and continued engagement with music throughout their lives.

SEND Curriculum
Our SEND curriculum is underpinned by the belief that every student is entitled to an ambitious, inclusive and high-quality education. We work collaboratively with students, families and staff to remove barriers to learning and enable students with additional needs to succeed across the curriculum.
We prioritise the development of resilience, empathy and independence, supporting students to understand their strengths and needs as learners. Through carefully planned interventions and in-class support, students are empowered to develop confidence, self-advocacy and strategies that promote long-term success.
A strong focus on literacy and communication enables students to access learning across subjects, engage meaningfully with texts and express ideas clearly. Support is adaptive and responsive, ensuring learning is accessible while maintaining high expectations.
Our SEND provision promotes inclusion, wellbeing and preparation for adulthood. By fostering independence and informed decision-making, we support students to make positive choices for their future. The SEND curriculum is designed not only to support academic progress, but to equip students with the skills, confidence and self-belief needed to thrive beyond school.

Governance
The Governors support the Trustees to fulfil their responsibility for oversight of each school within the Trust, acting as the eyes and ears of the Board at a local level. Their role is more focused than that of a traditional school governing body. The SAST central team manages – finance, HR, Estates, IT, and others.
The Governors responsibility is to monitor and scrutinise teaching and learning, welfare, and safeguarding issues. The Governors provide challenge and support to the Headteachers and senior leadership team, and represent the Trust to local stakeholders – parents, students, staff and the community. Two representatives of each Governing Body are elected from among that school’s parents, while a further representative will be elected by the staff. The Headteacher is ex officio. The remaining representatives are appointed by the Trustees following recommendations from the Governors and Headteacher, based on skills and experience.
The Governors will meet at the beginning of each full term (three times a year), plus an additional meeting to review published exam performance. Typically, this additional meeting will take place during the summer term for primary schools, once the SATS results have been published, whereas for secondary schools, this meeting will take place during the autumn term.

Prevent (radicalisation)
The Prevent strategy, published by the Government in 2011, is part of our overall counter-terrorism strategy, CONTEST. The aim of the Prevent strategy is to reduce the threat to the UK from terrorism by stopping people becoming terrorists or supporting terrorism. In the Act this has simply been expressed as the need to “prevent people from being drawn into terrorism”.
The 2011 Prevent strategy has three specific strategic objectives:
As children grow and become more independent, it is not unusual for them to take risks, explore new things and push boundaries. Teenage years are often a time when young people will be searching for answers to questions about identity, faith and belonging, as well as looking for adventure and excitement.
This can mean that they are particularly vulnerable to extremist groups, who may claim to offer answers, as well as identity and a strong social network. Due to the fact that they know young people are vulnerable, extremist groups often target them using the internet and social media to spread their ideology. There have been a number of tragic examples where young people have been misled by extremist groups, with some travelling to Syria and others becoming involved in hate crimes against minority groups.
Every member of staff at Sturminster Newton high school is trained to know the signs of a child who is vulnerable and possibly susceptible to becoming radicalised. As much as we educate our children to make the right choices in life it is impossible for us to monitor their decisions and the influences around them when they are outside of the school. It is therefore imperative that parents and carers are aware of who their children are talking to both online and face to face.
Let’s Talk About It is an initiative designed to provide practical help and guidance to the public in order to stop people becoming terrorists or supporting terrorism.
Let’s Talk About It has been created to provide a greater understanding of the support Prevent can offer and to challenge division and negativity in our communities through positive and effective attitude changes. By highlighting the issues and initiating discussions around the potential threats we face as a community, we can create greater understanding and wider awareness.

Art & Photography
The Art and Photography curriculum is designed to develop confident, creative and independent learners through a broad, skills-based and knowledge-rich programme of study. Students are taught to understand how artists, designers and photographers use materials, techniques and visual language to communicate ideas, emotions and meaning across cultures and time.
From Year 7, students build strong foundations in observational drawing, mark making, colour theory, tonal work, photography and presentation. Learning is carefully sequenced to develop procedural knowledge of materials and processes alongside declarative knowledge of artists, movements and cultural contexts. Students explore a wide range of disciplines including ceramics, cultural art, modern art movements and digital photography, using the work of key artists to inform and inspire their own creative responses.
As students progress through KS3 and KS4, they develop increasing independence through personalised projects, creative problem solving and reflective refinement of their work. GCSE and A-level courses extend this further through sustained studio practice, contextual research and disciplined experimentation, supporting ambition and high-quality outcomes.
Across all key stages, Art and Photography develop transferable skills such as resilience, critical thinking, collaboration and visual literacy. Students leave the subject equipped with creative confidence, cultural capital and the ability to communicate ideas visually, preparing them for further study, creative careers and lifelong engagement with the arts.

Computing
The Computing curriculum is designed to provide equitable access to a high-quality, future-focused education that empowers all students to succeed in a digital world. High expectations and careful sequencing ensure that knowledge and skills build progressively over time.
Students develop computational thinking, learning to decompose problems, apply logic and create effective solutions through programming and digital technologies. Digital literacy and online safety are central, enabling students to engage responsibly and confidently with technology.
The curriculum is structured to develop independence and resilience, encouraging students to learn from mistakes and adapt solutions. Practical application of knowledge supports creativity, problem-solving and innovation.
Computing prepares students to become confident users and creators of technology. By the time students leave school, they are equipped with the skills, knowledge and confidence needed for further study, employment and active participation in an increasingly technological society.

English
The English curriculum is underpinned by the belief that every student is entitled to an ambitious, inclusive and high-quality English education, regardless of background or starting point. Equity of provision is central to curriculum design, ensuring that all pupils experience consistently high expectations, carefully designed resources and high-quality teaching in every English classroom.
The curriculum is carefully sequenced to develop students’ reading, writing, speaking and thinking skills progressively over time. At Key Stage 3, pupils study a rich and diverse range of texts, including modern prose, non-fiction, poetry and Shakespeare, building strong foundations in literacy, analysis and creative expression. This structured progression prepares students for the increasing academic rigour of Key Stage 4.
Across all key stages, the curriculum explicitly teaches the knowledge, skills and strategies required for confident communication and critical thinking. Consistency in curriculum design, teaching approaches and expectations ensures that all pupils receive the same high standard of education.
English plays a vital role in students’ academic success and personal development. By the time students leave school, they are articulate, empathetic and reflective individuals, equipped with the literacy skills, cultural understanding and confidence needed for further study, employment and active participation in society.

Geography
The Geography curriculum is founded on the belief that every student is entitled to a high-quality, ambitious and carefully sequenced education that enables them to understand the world and their place within it. High expectations and equitable access ensure that all students can succeed, regardless of starting point.
The curriculum is structured to develop secure knowledge of physical and human geography, building progressively from local to global contexts. Students explore landscapes, environments, populations and global interdependence, developing understanding of key concepts such as place, scale, sustainability and change. Learning is sequenced so that knowledge is revisited and deepened over time, supporting long-term retention.
Geographical enquiry is central to the subject. Students learn to interpret maps, data and case studies, apply geographical skills and evaluate issues from multiple perspectives. Through discussion and investigation, they develop critical thinking and informed judgement.
Geography supports students to become environmentally and socially responsible global citizens. By the time students leave school, they are equipped with geographical knowledge, analytical skills and cultural awareness that prepare them for further study, employment and informed participation in an increasingly interconnected world.

History
The History curriculum ensures that all students have equitable access to an ambitious and knowledge-rich understanding of the past. High expectations underpin learning, enabling students to think critically, question evidence and develop a secure sense of chronology.
The curriculum is carefully sequenced to build historical knowledge over time, enabling students to understand key events, individuals and developments in local, national and global contexts. Concepts such as causation, consequence, similarity and difference are revisited and deepened, supporting coherent historical understanding.
Students are taught to analyse sources, evaluate interpretations and construct reasoned arguments supported by evidence. Through debate and enquiry, they learn to challenge assumptions and consider diverse perspectives.
History develops analytical thinking, communication and reasoning skills that extend beyond the classroom. By the time students leave school, they are confident historians with the knowledge and skills to understand the present through the lens of the past and to engage thoughtfully as informed citizens.

Maths
At Sturminster Newton High School, the Mathematics curriculum is built on the principles of honesty, effort and high expectations for all. We are committed to providing an ambitious, inclusive and carefully sequenced curriculum that ensures equity of provision, so that every student experiences high-quality teaching and learning in every mathematics classroom they enter.
Our curriculum is designed to develop concentration, attention to detail and critical thinking, enabling students to become confident, fluent and resilient mathematicians. Through a coherent and well-sequenced curriculum from Key Stage 3 to Key Stage 5, students build secure mathematical knowledge that deepens over time, allowing them to make connections between concepts and apply their learning with accuracy and confidence.
We aim for all students to have a positive experience of mathematics, developing both numeracy and mathematical literacy that equips them for everyday life and future study. Lessons are carefully planned to support all learners, while also providing appropriate challenge to stretch and inspire. We place strong emphasis on reasoning, problem solving and mathematical communication, ensuring students can articulate their thinking clearly and logically.
Mathematics opens the door to a wide range of STEM pathways, and our curriculum is designed to raise aspirations and prepare students to progress successfully. Through consistent expectations, expert teaching and purposeful assessment, we support every student to achieve their very best in mathematics and to leave school inspired, confident and prepared for the next stage of their learning.

PSHE
The PSHE curriculum reflects the belief that all students are entitled to a high-quality, inclusive education that prepares them for life beyond school. High expectations and equity underpin learning, ensuring students develop confidence, resilience and self-awareness.
The curriculum is carefully sequenced to address physical and mental health, relationships, safety, citizenship and future pathways in an age-appropriate manner. Knowledge and skills are built progressively, enabling students to make informed decisions and manage increasing responsibility.
PSHE supports personal development by fostering empathy, self-efficacy and the ability to seek support when needed. Lessons provide a safe environment for discussion, reflection and exploration of real-life challenges.
By the time students leave school, they are equipped with the knowledge, skills and understanding needed to manage wellbeing, relationships and responsibilities, preparing them to contribute positively to their communities and wider society.

Religious Education
The Religious Education curriculum is rooted in the belief that every student is entitled to an inclusive and ambitious exploration of beliefs, values and worldviews. High expectations ensure that all students engage thoughtfully and respectfully with complex ideas.
The curriculum is carefully sequenced to develop knowledge of religious and non-religious worldviews over time. Students explore beliefs, practices and ethical questions, revisiting key concepts to deepen understanding and promote critical reflection.
RE provides a safe and respectful space for discussion, enabling students to articulate ideas, listen to others and consider different perspectives. Students develop skills of interpretation, evaluation and reflection as they explore life’s big questions.
Religious Education supports moral, social and cultural development. By the time students leave school, they are equipped with empathy, respect and critical awareness, enabling them to engage positively with diversity and contribute thoughtfully to society.
